**Answer: 16**

**Upper bound.** Fix a colour and let $S$ be the set of squares painted with it. Every square in $S$ has at least two orthogonal neighbours in $S$, so the subgraph of the grid graph induced by $S$ has minimum degree at least 2. A graph with minimum degree at least 2 contains a cycle. The grid graph is bipartite, so every cycle in it has even length, at least 4. Hence $|S| \ge 4$.

Since the 64 squares are partitioned among the colours, and each colour class has at least 4 squares, the number of colours satisfies $4k \le 64$, so $k \le 16$.

**Construction.** Divide the board into sixteen disjoint $2\times 2$ blocks and paint each block a different colour. In a $2\times 2$ block, each square is orthogonally adjacent to exactly two other squares of the block, and both share its colour. So every square has two same-coloured neighbours, and 16 colours are used.

Therefore the maximum is 16.

ANSWER: 16
